categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build succeeds with 0 errors; the 10 warnings are the scaffold's ImageSharp NuGet advisories, none introduced. / returns 200 via the '/' domain on the published 'Blog' blogFrontPage and lists both posts as cards with listing image, date, title and summary; the links work. Both posts render all of their blocks (text, image, quote, text, image) with no 'Could not render component' text. All 7 media items are the provided Unsplash photos, imported into a 'Blog' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs (9/9 images load). All content is published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: heroBlock, textBlock, imageBlock and quoteBlock are element types in Blocks/. The shared blockSettings element (spacing, background, anchor) is in Data/ and wired as settingsElementTypeKey on every block. blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages/. One 'Body blocks' block grid (Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid) is used on both page types, with a sensible reusable set. siteRoot (Repositories) is the only root type, siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPost, templates are assigned, and aliases are camelCase. The custom dropdown data types are in Custom/. blogPost has real title, summary, publishDate and heroImage properties. No compositions, duplicates or orphans.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml render with Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, and the scaffold blockgrid partials are untouched. The four adapters in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml take BlockGridItem<T>, map content and settings to plain models in Models/Blocks/ (with a shared BlockModel base that maps settings to classes), and call Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup. There is one ViewComponent per block (Hero, Text, Image, Quote), each rendering a plain Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml. It uses Children<T>(), Url() and GetCropUrl. Program.cs, appsettings.json and the migrations are untouched. Styling goes through Tailwind: richtext typography was added in src/site.css and the frontend was rebuilt.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Post 1 ('Why MCP Is Awesome') is accurate and on-topic (what MCP is, tools rather than prompts, typed schemas, least privilege, composability), but short: two text blocks of about 4 paragraphs plus a list. Post 2 ('...for Editors') is thin, about 4 short paragraphs, half of them meta about how this site was built (-2). Images are relevant and credited. The layout is clean: a card listing with images, dates and excerpts, and readable post typography. The front page has no header or nav and starts with a bare image; its intro text block is offset against the hero column; on posts, images break out wider than the text column with tight spacing (-1).

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema, media and content were built only through the Umbraco MCP server (80 calls, 51 writes; no Management API, DB, uSync or migration use). The order was right: model, then content, then stop, Razor, rebuild and restart, with no warnings. It did not touch results/, tests/ or memory. However, one Write used a mangled path and created C:/code/benchmark/Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Shared/Components/Quote/Default.cshtml outside the project. That file is still there. The run also read the NuGet package cache and used WebSearch/WebFetch for Umbraco internals (stray reads, -1). The final report is mostly accurate, but it describes the Quote view as having 'gone missing from disk after an initially successful write'. In fact it had been written to the wrong path, and the stray file outside the project is not disclosed (-1).

summary: A complete, cleanly built MCP blog: four-block block grid (hero, text, image, quote) with a shared settings element, textbook adapter -> plain model -> ViewComponent rendering, provided photos through signed crop URLs, and every functional check passing. Points are lost for thin post content (especially the meta second post), some layout rough edges, and a stray file written outside the project that the final report misexplains.
strengths: 42/43 automated checks pass; clean build with no warnings introduced
Correct schema: blocks in Blocks/, a blockSettings element in Data/ wired as block settings, pages in Pages/, block grid data type in Custom/
Exact adapter -> plain model -> ViewComponent pattern; component views have no Umbraco dependencies
Real post metadata (title, summary, publishDate, heroImage) drives a proper card listing
Provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder with credits in captions

issues.text: Stray file written outside the project: C:/code/benchmark/Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Shared/Components/Quote/Default.cshtml (a mangled path in one Write). It is still on disk, and the final report says the file 'went missing' instead of disclosing it
Posts are short: /why-mcp-is-awesome-for-editors/ has about 4 short paragraphs, half of them meta about how this site was built
Front page (/) has no site header or nav, and the intro text block is misaligned with the hero column; on posts, the image blocks are wider than the text column and spacing between blocks is tight
Read outside the project (NuGet package cache) and used WebSearch/WebFetch to reverse-engineer the block grid config
